text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Deputy Justice Minister Nguyen Van San says the amended Criminal Code is vivid proof of Vietnam's determination to be stricter in dealing with corruption, drug-related crimes and sexual exploitation of children.
-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi told a visiting high-ranking Cuban military delegation that Vietnam will always be at Cuba's side.
-- The Asia Development Bank's President Mitsuo Sato has said the ADB plans to provide Vietnam with annual soft loans of about $350 million during the period 1998-2000.

-- The government has approved the budget for a specialized medical centre in Ho Chi Minh City to meet the demand of Vietnamese citizens and foreigners for high-quality emergency, diagnostic and treatment services.
-- About 1,500 households living along canals in Ho Chi Minh City will be relocated this year.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet concluded his trip to Italy on Tuesday and headed for Hungary.
-- Vice Prime Minister Tran Duc Luong has been appointed as chairman of the National Committee on air and sea rescue.
-- Vietnam's consumer prices dropped by 0.5 percent in May from April levels.
-- Commercial Services Departments in Hanoi, Hue and Ho Chi Minh City have agreed to a regular exchange of experience in State management of business activities and market operations.
-- Ho Chi Minh City's Party Chief, Truong Tan Sang, has asked Vietnam Electricity to ensure a safe and continuous power supply to the city.
